summary: Describes an IMAP extension for sorting messages on the server by the displayed part of the From and To header fields, such as a person's name. It is a Proposed Standard.

plainLanguage.summary: Sorting your mail by the name you see, not the hidden address.

subtitle: IMAP sort criteria that order messages by the name people see in From and To, not the bare address.

tldr.problem: The IMAP SORT extension sorts FROM and TO on the bare mailbox part of the first address, which is not what users see in their message lists.
tldr.mechanism: Two new sort criteria, DISPLAYFROM and DISPLAYTO, sort on the address's display name when present, falling back to the mailbox address; servers advertise SORT=DISPLAY.
tldr.outcome: It updates RFC 5256 and adds one capability to the IMAP registry.

today: RFC 5957 is a Proposed Standard that updates RFC 5256. No later RFC is listed as obsoleting or updating it.

sections.title: Introduction
sections.content:
The SORT extension (RFC 5256) to IMAP (RFC 3501) lets the server sort messages. Its FROM and TO orderings sort lexically on the addr-mailbox of the first address in the From and To headers.

This document adds DISPLAYFROM and DISPLAYTO, which sort on the first address's addr-name (generally the display-name) when present. A server supporting full SORT and both criteria returns SORT=DISPLAY in its CAPABILITY response.
sections.plainLanguage: Mail used to be sorted by the hidden address. Now it can be sorted by the name you actually see.

sections.title: How the Sort Value Is Chosen
sections.content:
For an address, the sort value comes from the first rule that applies. If addr-name is non-NIL, decode any RFC 2047 encoded-words and convert the result into a charset valid for the active collation (default UTF-8), as in RFC 5255; if that is not empty, use it. Otherwise, if mailbox and host are both non-NIL, use addr-mailbox@addr-host. Otherwise, if only the mailbox is non-NIL, use it. Otherwise the value is the empty string.

For a message, take the envelope from FETCH ENVELOPE. DISPLAYFROM uses env-from and DISPLAYTO uses env-to. If that value is NIL the sort value is the empty string; otherwise it is the sort value of the first address in it.
sections.plainLanguage: Use the person's name if there is one; if not, use their email address; if there is nothing, use blank.

sections.title: Syntax and Internationalization
sections.content:
The ABNF adds SORT=DISPLAY to capability and DISPLAYFROM and DISPLAYTO to sort-key.

Both criteria are string-based, so the active collation MUST be used. They sort on the full decoded addr-name and do not try to pick out a meaningful part such as the surname.
sections.plainLanguage: The sorting looks at the whole name as written, not just the last name.

sections.title: Security and IANA
sections.content:
The extension only adds an IMAP capability, so it does not change the underlying security considerations of IMAP. The author believes no new security issues are introduced.

IANA registration: this document registers the SORT=DISPLAY capability in the IMAP capabilities registry.
sections.plainLanguage: It is only a new way to sort, so it adds no new risk, and the new name goes on the official list.

viz.caption: ORDER OF RULES FOR AN ADDRESS SORT VALUE

items.label: addr-name
items.desc: Decoded display name, if non-NIL and not empty.

items.label: mailbox@host
items.desc: If addr-mailbox and addr-host are both non-NIL.

items.label: empty string
items.desc: If none of the above apply.
